speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. I need to know if you or your family have a history of bleeding disorders. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Plating.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL, Platelets: 280,000 /μL (normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood test results show your platelet count is normal, which rules out common platelet disorders. Since you have mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae with normal platelets, do you bruise easily or have bleeding after minor injuries? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Coagulation_Profile: PT: 12 seconds (normal), aPTT: 30 seconds (normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: The coagulation profile is normal, so a clotting factor deficiency is unlikely. Since you have mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae but your platelet count and clotting times are normal, do you experience excessive bleeding after dental work or surgery? REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Assay.

speaker: Doctor
text: The tests confirm your platelets, clotting factors, and von Willebrand factor are all normal, which is unusual given your bleeding symptoms. Have you noticed any specific foods in your diet that might be affecting your health? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Test.

speaker: Doctor
text: The liver function tests are normal, so liver disease is not the cause of your bleeding. Have you experienced any recent viral infections, or do you have a fever and fatigue? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Test; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP) - Chronic or Atypical presentation; however, given the completely normal platelet count, coagulation profile, von Willebrand factor, and liver function despite mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae, this is most consistent with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) or a localized vascular anomaly, but without a family history of telangiectasias or AVMs confirmed, further imaging of the mucosa is required.
